CadAssistance.heading: Don't have a CAD file? We'll draw it for you.
CadAssistance.subheading: Send a sketch, a photo, or just the dimensions over WhatsApp — our team returns a manufacturing-ready CAD file you can quote and produce right away.
CadAssistance.step1Copy: A hand sketch, a photo of the part, or a list of dimensions — straight over WhatsApp.
CadAssistance.step2Copy: Our team turns it into a manufacturing-ready STEP/IGES file within 48 hours.
CadAssistance.step3Copy: Use the file to get a quote and put the part into production — all in one place.
CadAssistance.tier3Desc: From a physical sample or broken part

HowItWorks.heading: From upload to delivery.
HowItWorks.intro: Every order follows the same clear path — you send a design, we handle the rest.
HowItWorks.step1Copy: Send us your STL, STEP, DXF, or IGES file with quantity, material, and any notes.
HowItWorks.step2Copy: We identify the right process for your part — 3D printing, CNC machining, laser cutting, or EDM.
HowItWorks.step3Copy: We route the job to a vetted partner workshop and track it through production.
HowItWorks.step4Copy: Your finished part is quality-checked and delivered back to you.

About.heading: Manufacturing, made simple in Qatar.
About.lead: Gestaltung for Trading and Services is a manufacturing marketplace and inventory platform based in Lusail, Qatar.
About.body1: We connect clients who need parts made with the network of skilled workshops that can make them. You send a design; we match it to the right production method and a capable Qatari workshop, then manage the job through to delivery.
About.body2: Alongside custom manufacturing, we run a store for high-quality mechanical parts and a multi-tenant inventory system that keeps every workshop's and client's data cleanly separated.
About.value1Copy: The right method for every part, not a one-size-fits-all process.
About.value2Copy: Vetted workshops across Qatar, coordinated in one place.
About.value3Copy: Track every job and every item from one bilingual dashboard.

Prototyping.metaDescription: Take a rough idea to a manufacturable product: a brief, a part breakdown with materials and processes, and 2D schematics.
Prototyping.openIntro: Break this project into parts, pick materials and processes, and generate 2D schematics.
Prototyping.stageTitle_idea: Describe what you want to make
Prototyping.stageDesc_parts: Each part needs a material and a process from our production network. Suggestions are never applied until you confirm them.
Prototyping.openItems: {count, plural, =0 {Nothing open} one {# open item} other {# open items}}
Prototyping.briefIntro: Write it the way you would explain it to an engineer.
Prototyping.briefPlaceholder: What is it, where does it live, what does it have to survive, how many do you need?
Prototyping.briefTooShort: Write a little more first — a sentence or two about what it is.
Prototyping.reanalyseWarn: Re-analysing replaces suggestions you have not confirmed. Confirmed and edited items are kept.
Prototyping.claimsIntro: Read from your brief by a rules engine, not a person. Confirm each point or correct it.
Prototyping.noClaims: Nothing yet. Write a brief and analyse it.
Prototyping.nothingApplied: Nothing is applied until you confirm it.
Prototyping.claim_outdoor: It lives outdoors, so treat it as weather-exposed equipment.
Prototyping.claim_heat: It has to survive Gulf summer heat — plan for 50 °C ambient and direct sun.
Prototyping.claim_washdown: It gets washed or hosed down, so surfaces must not rust or trap water.
Prototyping.claim_solar: It runs off-grid on solar with a battery.
Prototyping.claim_power: It needs a power source — we assumed one; tell us which.
Prototyping.claim_electronics: It needs a custom electronics board rather than off-the-shelf modules.
Prototyping.claim_batch: You need a batch of {count} units.
Prototyping.claim_batch_unknown: We could not find a quantity — we assumed a small batch. How many do you need?
Prototyping.claim_security: It must resist tampering in a public place.
Prototyping.claim_mounting: We assumed it is fixed in place rather than portable.
Prototyping.noParts: No parts yet. Analyse the brief, or add one by hand.
Prototyping.addPartSub: Describe it. We can suggest a material and process — you decide whether to use them.
Prototyping.reason_precision: the tight feature needs EDM to hold tolerance without distortion
Prototyping.reason_sheet: it is a flat or bent panel
Prototyping.reason_shaped: it is a shaped part in low volume
Prototyping.reason_generic: it is a small structural part
Prototyping.part_enclosure_desc: The outer body. Cut flat, then bent — cheap at low volume and strong once folded.
Prototyping.part_roof_desc: Carries the solar panel and shades the body.
Prototyping.part_dispenser_desc: The moving feed path. Printed so the internal shape can follow the mechanism.
Prototyping.part_reservoir_desc: Holds the liquid side. Rounded so it can be cleaned properly.
Prototyping.part_bracket_desc: Fixes the unit in place. Slotted so it can be adjusted on site.
Prototyping.part_pcb_desc: The custom electronics: microcontroller, sensors and drivers on one board.
Prototyping.part_coupling_desc: Connects the motor to the moving part. Needs a tight tolerance.
Prototyping.part_body_desc: The main structural part. Edit this once you know the shape.
Prototyping.part_plate_desc: A flat base to mount everything to.
Prototyping.recIntro: Recomputed from your current parts every time you change one.
Prototyping.recEmpty: Confirm some parts and a route appears here.
Prototyping.warn_unset: {code} {name}: no material or process chosen yet.
Prototyping.warn_incompatible: {code} {name}: {material} cannot be made with {process} in our network.
Prototyping.warn_pla_heat: {code} {name}: PLA softens around 55 °C — use PETG or ABS outdoors here.
Prototyping.warn_steel_rust: {code} {name}: mild steel rusts when it gets wet unless it is coated — stainless avoids the extra step.
Prototyping.warn_acrylic_brittle: {code} {name}: acrylic goes brittle in sun and heat.
Prototyping.warn_wood_wet: {code} {name}: plywood and MDF swell when they get wet.
Prototyping.schIntro: Drawn from the part you confirmed. These are for discussion and mark-up, not manufacturing files.
